finding: The operator's intuition is RIGHT and mostly ALREADY CAPTURED — but via the FLOATER, not duration. EASING (live regime 2025-06-06->2026-06-10): the OFZ FLOATER (RUFLBITR, which the SAA HOLDS as its OFZ_PK leg) returned 16.67% vs the deposit's 13.7% — it OUT-carries the deposit by ~3.0pp (a bond at ~key beats a deposit at key-1pp). So 'bonds beat the deposit' shows up in the system through the floater. HOWEVER fixed-coupon OFZ (duration) returned only 12.25% — it did NOT beat the deposit or the floater in this easing, because the curve was INVERTED (short rates > long yields), so locking a lower long yield gave up carry AND took a 6.22% duration drawdown. HIKING (2023-24): fixed OFZ TR=-9.3% vs deposit 19.57% — fixed LOSES badly (price losses as rates rose). So the iter-1 gate's fixed-OFZ REJECT HOLDS even per-regime — locking duration was not the winning trade. THE GENUINE GAP: the system's floater FALLS with the key, so it does NOT LOCK today's 15-16% for the future. IF you can now buy a FIXED 15-16% bond above the 14%-and-falling deposit AND the curve has un-inverted, locking that carry is a real forward call the floater can't make — but it carries duration risk and, on the realized easing here, the floater's high short carry beat it. Not advice; diagnostic only.
